title: autotune: default batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Jordan Carter
description: Summary: Add end-to-end autotune for batching and KV-prefix caching defaults, introduce quantization profile management for model variants, and a unit-economics dashboard + CLI tooling to evaluate per-token cost impact. Motivation: Customers frequently ask for better out-of-the-box cost controls. We observed a 20-40% variance in unit economics across deployments because teams either keep conservative batching/caching settings or manually tune per-model. This PR introduces: 1) autotune service that observes request latency and tail-latency SLOs and suggests/rolls out batching and caching defaults per route; 2) quantization profile registry and safer deploy path to test model-quality vs throughput tradeoffs; 3) unit-econ tooling (dashboard and dry-run CLI) that simulates expected token cost and latency for candidate policies. Changes include runtime hooks, a small scheduler change to support dynamic batch-size caps, metric emitters, console dashboard pages, and a CLI tool to run policy dry-runs against historical traces. Checklist: - [x] Autotune controller + policies implemented - [x] Runtime batching/caching hooks and config APIs - [x] Quantization profile schema + registry + migration - [x] Unit-econ backend + console pages - [x] CLI dry-run and report generation - [x] Integration tests and e2e perf runs - [x] Docs and migration notes (redwood-docs PR linked) See also: Linear ENG-4821, ENG-4875; design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/documents/autotune-batching-design. Impact: Gradual rollout via canary routes, default off for existing customers. New tenants get safe defaults enabled. Migration notes: run `redwood uecon migrate-profiles` to populate profiles for existing models. Configuration: new per-route fields `autotune.enabled`, `autotune.target_tail_ms`, `autotune.max_batch_tokens`, `quant.profile`.
commits: Initial implementation of autotune controller and metrics emitter
Add runtime hooks for dynamic batch caps and KV cache defaults
Unit-econ backend, CLI and console pages
Integration tests and perf harness updates
diff_snippets:
--- a/core/runtime/batching.py
+++ b/core/runtime/batching.py
@@ -42,6 +42,12 @@ def select_batch_size(reqs):
-    return min(global_max, heuristic(reqs))
+    # respect dynamic cap from autotune controller
+    dynamic_cap = config.get('autotune.max_batch_tokens', global_max)
+    cap = min(global_max, dynamic_cap)
+    return min(cap, heuristic(reqs))
review_comments: Priya Natarajan (reviewer): This looks great overall. A few nits and one concern about race conditions when the controller updates the cap while a batch is in progress. Please add a short doc on the locking semantics.
Jordan Carter (author): Added a lock and retry backoff in batching runtime. See batching.py + comments. Also added integration test that simulates concurrent updates.
Lena Ortiz (reviewer): Can we add a smoke test for the CLI in CI? The uecon dry-run is useful but brittle with large traces.
Jordan Carter (author): Added lightweight smoke test in CI and a synthetic small-trace fixture. CI flakeyness reduced.
Marco Silva (approver): Verified perf run (canary) shows median latency unchanged and 18% avg cost reduction for typical chat workload. Approving.
perf_summary: Canary perf (2-week run on staging): average token cost -18% across chat workloads, p99 latency within configured SLO (target_tail_ms = 250ms) for 98.6% of requests. Observed improved GPU utilization with batching cap adjustments.
rollback_plan: Autotune controller changes are gated behind feature flag 'autotune_v1'. If we see regression, flip feature flag off which will revert to previous static defaults. Quant profile registry supports fallback to unquantized variant. Unit-econ reports included to help root-cause.
release_notes: Add autotune controller for batching/caching defaults, quantization profile registry, and unit-economics tooling (CLI + console). Opt-in via per-route `autotune.enabled`. Provides recommended defaults and dry-run cost simulations.
